locations.name: Santa Fe Community Center & Courtyard Facility
locations.fit: Accommodates both the interior dance rehearsal space ('COMMUNITY HALL') and the adjacent exterior 'COURTYARD' within a single property footprint, minimizing company moves between Scenes 1, 2, and 3.
risks: Filming permits must be applied for and approved through local jurisdiction prior to production; availability is not guaranteed.
Santa Fe municipal filming regulations require application fees ($25 small / $100 large) plus $10 per shoot day regardless of public or private property status.
General liability insurance meeting regional/municipal thresholds ($1,050,000 standard NM requirement / $1M minimum) must be secured and submitted prior to access confirmation.
Facility floor safety and spatial clearance for dance choreography require on-site technical scout verification.

risks: Permitting must be coordinated via Film Las Cruces; access and schedule availability require verification.
Nearby resident and business notification within a standard 200-foot radius is likely required 48 hours in advance of load-in.
Proof of standard general liability insurance coverage is required before permit issuance and property entry can occur.
Exterior daylight conditions and acoustic control between the hall and courtyard must be verified during scouting.

Filming activities may be interrupted if you fail to obtain written permission from the railroad owner to enter its property. research.title: New Mexico Film Permits: 3 Important Permitting Facts - PPS
research.excerpt: Requirements New Mexico Film Permits Request Permit Consultation New Mexico Film Permit Requirements What are the permit requirements to film in New Mexico\ \ Filming in New Mexico requires securing the appropriate New Mexico film permits to ensure that production activities comply with state and local laws. These permits are typically required for filming on public property, streets, or any other public spaces, and they help to regulate access to filming locations. Filmmakers must provide detailed information about the project, including location, dates, times, and the nature of the filming activities. It’s essential to apply for New Mexico film permits in advance to avoid any last-minute complications and to ensure that all necessary permits are in place before production begins. Filmmakers must work closely with local authorities to meet these requirements and avoid fines or delays. The permit process also ensures that filmmakers maintain the safety of their crew, cast, and the public during filming, which is crucial when filming in public spaces or urban environments. Filmmakers should also be prepared for additional permitting requirements if they plan to film in certain special locations in New Mexico, such as national parks, monuments, or other protected areas. These areas often have strict environmental regulations, and additional New Mexico film permits may be required to film in these locations. Productions that impact the environment or use natural features for their scenes must ensure they meet all the required criteria to protect New Mexico’s natural resources. Permits for these areas are typically more detailed and require advanced planning to ensure compliance.

research.title: Permits - Film Las Cruces
research.excerpt: Film Las Cruces is contracted with the City of Las Cruces, Doña Ana County and the City of Anthony to provide permitting assistance to film and digital media projects. We are happy to walk you through and point you in the right direction for all other permitting agencies throughout southern New Mexico; including White Sands National Park, Town of Mesilla, Bureau of Land Management, Spaceport America, Hatch, New Mexico Department of Transportation, and others. What kinds of filming activities do not require a permit? News and gathering of news related stories. Other types of documentaries not requiring the use of actors, models, sets, or props. Still not sure if your production requires a filming permit? Give us a call: 575-805-3456 What is a low impact/b-roll permit? A low impact/b-roll filming permit may be issued for documentary-style footage with a maximum of 8 total cast and crew on-site at any one time. When should I notify neighboring residents and businesses regarding filming activity in the area? All permitted filming locations are likely to require the surrounding businesses and neighbors to be notified of your filming activity 48 hours in advance of load in. The standard radius for notification letter distribution is 200 feet from the filming location, parking, and basecamp. Film Las Cruces will notify your production with notification requirements during the process of your application. From film financing for production companies to basic training for crew members , the State of New Mexico Film Office acts as a conduit between filmmakers and whatever resources they require.
